div.head: III Eg 8
div.ab: ⁊ ga an mynet ofer ealne þæs cynges anweald, ⁊ þane nan man ne forsace;
⁊ gange án mynet ofer ealne ðæs cynges anweald, ⁊ þæne nan man ne forsace.
⁊ gange án mynet ofer ealne þæs cyninges anweald, ⁊ þone nan man ne forsace.
⁊ gange an mynet ofer ealne þæs cynges anweald, ⁊ þæne nan man ne forsace.
Et sit una moneta per totum regis imperium, et nemo sonet eam;
[Be mynetum ⁊ gemettum.] ⁊ gange án mynet ofer ealne þæs cyninges anweald, ⁊ þone nan man ne forsace.
And ga an mynet ofer ealne þæs cynges anweald, and þane nan man ne forsace.
(Von Münzen und Maassen. Ld) Und es gehe Eine Münze über des Königs ganzes Gebiet, und die weise niemand zurück;
(Of coins and measures. Ld) And let one coinage be current throughout all the king's dominion, and let no one refuse it;
And one coinage shall be current throughout all the king's realm, and no-one shall refuse it.
And one coinage is to be current throughout all the king’s dominion, and no man is to refuse it;
And there is to be one coinage throughout the king’s whole realm and no one may refuse it.

note.seg: Aus 8 und 8, 1 floss wahrscheinlich IV Atr 6 = VI 32, 1f. = II Cn 8f. Vgl. Gl Münze 3. 10; Münzfälschung 2c
IV Atr 6 = VI 32, 1f. = II Cn 8f. probably derived from 8 and 8, 1. Cf. Gl Münze 3. 10; Münzfälschung 2c

Dies wiederholen z. T. IV Atr 6. II Cn 8, wo Q repudiare überträgt. Also ist auch hier sein sonare nicht von sonus ‘Ton’ abzuleiten, sondern mit absoniare, das er Swer 1 für ascunian setzt, zu verbinden. Auch im sonstigen Normanno-Latein (Somma de leg. Norm. ed. 1523, c. 123) heisst sconare ‘verwerfen’.—Auf Nichtannahme der novi denarii setzt Geldstrafe Capit. Francfurt. a. 794 ed. Boretius (Mon. Germ.) I 74, 5

This is repeated in part by IV Atr 6. II Cn 8, where Q renders it as repudiare. So here too his sonare is not to be derived from sonus ‘sound’, but to be connected with absoniare, which he puts for ascunian in Swer 1. In other Norman Latin too (Somma de leg. Norm. ed. 1523, c. 123) sconare means ‘reject’. — A money fine for refusing to accept the novi denarii is imposed by Capit. Francfurt. a. 794 ed. Boretius (Mon. Germ.) I 74, 5
Cf. II As. 14; IV Atr. 6; VI, 32, 1; II Cn. 8.

See Chadwick, op. cit. p. 34 for a table showing the weight of Edgar’s coins as compared with those of his predecessors and successors. Matthew Paris, ann. 975 (Rolls Series, i. p. 467), notes the issue of a new coinage at the end of his reign: deinde per totam Angliam nouam fieri praecepit monetam, quia uetus uitio tonsorum adeo erat corrupta ut uix nummus obolum appenderet in statera. See Chadwick, op. cit. pp. 36, 38¹.
